title: The Pythagorean Theorem and Geometry
text: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the square of the length of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c². It is named after the ancient Greek philosopher Pythagoras, though it was known to Babylonian mathematicians over 1,000 years earlier. The theorem has hundreds of known proofs. In geometry, the theorem extends to the distance formula in coordinate geometry and to the law of cosines in non-right triangles. Non-Euclidean geometries, such as those on the surface of a sphere, do not obey the Pythagorean theorem.
